title: What Does the Bible Say About Dinosaurs? 26 Verses
description: Are dinosaurs in the Bible? The word is not there. What Genesis, Job's Behemoth and Leviathan, and the Psalms say about ancient creatures, with 26 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about dinosaurs
summary: The word dinosaur does not appear in the Bible. It was coined in 1842 by the English anatomist Richard Owen, and neither the World English Bible nor the King James Version uses it. The Bible does describe creatures made on the fifth and sixth days of creation (Genesis 1:20-25) and two great beasts in the book of Job: Behemoth, named once in Job 40:15, and Leviathan, named in 5 verses of the WEB. Whether these are dinosaurs, hippos, elephants, crocodiles or poetic images is argued by Christians: young-earth readers often see dinosaurs in Behemoth, while others read the Genesis days as long ages with dinosaurs among the creatures God made. The word dragon is also a translation split, 13 verses in the WEB and 34 in the KJV. The verses below are the ones that bear on the question.

faqs.q: Are dinosaurs mentioned in the Bible?
faqs.a: Not by name. The word dinosaur was coined in 1842, long after the Bible was written. Some Christians identify Behemoth (Job 40:15-24) or Leviathan (Job 41) with dinosaurs, because Behemoth is described with a tail like a cedar. Other readers identify Behemoth with a hippopotamus or elephant and Leviathan with a crocodile, or take both as poetic images of God's power over creation.

faqs.q: What is Behemoth in the Bible?
faqs.a: Behemoth is a huge animal God describes to Job: it eats grass like an ox, has strength in its loins, and is the first of God's works (Job 40:15-19). The name appears once in the Bible. Readers have taken it as a hippo, an elephant, a dinosaur or a symbol of chaos tamed by God.

faqs.q: Does the Bible say how old the earth is?
faqs.a: It does not give a number. Genesis 1 describes six days of creation, and Christians read the days differently: as six 24-hour days (young-earth view), as long periods (old-earth view), or as a literary frame. Psalm 90:2 and 2 Peter 3:8 are often cited in the discussion, and neither settles it.

faqs.q: Did dinosaurs die in the flood?
faqs.a: The Bible does not mention dinosaurs, so it does not say. Young-earth Christians teach that dinosaurs were on the ark and died out afterward. Old-earth Christians place their extinction millions of years before humans. The text of Genesis 6-9 speaks of the animals on the ark and the creatures that perished, without naming kinds.
